2501:
**Ἰωσήφ ** indecl.
(FlJ, Ἰώσηπος, -ου), ὁ (Heb. יוֹסֵף),
**Joseph**;
1. **the Son of Jacob**: Jhn.4:5, Act.7:9, 13-14 7:18, Heb.11:21-22, Rev.7:8.
2. In the genealogy of our Lord,
(a) **the son of Matthias**: Luk.3:24;
(b) **the son Joram**: Luk.3:30.
3. The husband of Mary, the Lord's mother Mat.1:16 ff, Luk.1:27, Jhn.1:46, al.
4. **One of the brethren of our Lord **(see: ἀδελφός): Mat.13:55.
5. **Son of Mary**: Mat.27:56 (-σῆς, WH, mg., RV).
6. **Joseph of Arimatbæa**: Mat.27:57, 59, Mrk.15:43, 45, Luk.23:50, Jhn.19:38.
7. see: Βαρνάβας.
8. see: Βαρσαβᾶς
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)

2512:
** κᾰθαρ-ισμός**, ὁ,

2517:
** καθεξῆς**,
_adverb_, = the more usually ἐφεξῆς, {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.Luke.1.3, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.615c, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Varia Historia” 8.7, “IGRom.” 4.1432.9 (from Smyrna)}}; _poetry_ κατά θ᾽ ἑξείης {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 3.59.}}
2522:
** καθημέρ-ιος**,
_Doric dialect_ **καθᾱμ-**, α, ον, **day by day, daily** (καθ᾽ ἡμέραν), _neuter_ as _adverb_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 229 (Lyric poetry)}}; μοῖρα κ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1414 (uncertain, Lyric poetry)}}:—later also **καθημερινός**, ή, όν, δίαιτα {{LXX+1st c.AD+|LXX.Jdt.12.15, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.141b, +others; διακονία NT.Act.6.1; γυμνασία 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “Tactica - Griechische Kriegsschriftsteller” 3.1, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 10, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 1.10c}}; of fevers, **quotidian**, later word for ἀμφημερινός (which see), especially of **non-remittent quotidians**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 7.354, 17(1).221; ῥῖγος “PTeb.” 275.21 (3rd c.AD)}}; φρίξ {{Refs 4th c.AD+|“POxy.” 924.3 (4th c.AD).}}
2530:
** καθότι**,
_Ionic dialect_ **κατ-**, for καθ᾽ ὅ τι (which should perhaps be written) **in what manner,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|Inscriptiones Graecae 12.24.8, +others, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.2, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.82, etc.}}; κ. γέγραπται **as** is written, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“SIG” 577.18 (Milet., 3rd-2nd c.BC)}}, etc.; **so far as, inasmuch as**, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.25.3, +others}}

2551:
** κᾰκολογ-έω**,
**revile, abuse**, τινα {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 8.5, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.98, 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 25, LXX.Exo.21.16(17), NT.Matt.15.4, +others: _absolutely_, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 36.61}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Gorgias Rhetor et Sophista “Hel.” 7, “PFay.” 12.15 (2nd c.BC).}}
2552:
** κᾰκοπάθ-εια** [πᾰ], ἡ,
**distress, misery**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 10, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.2.11, Isocrates 6.55, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1278b28; σώματος 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.18}}; of plants or trees, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.7.8}}; **strain, stress**, on the parts of a machine, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Belopoeica” 93.1: _plural_, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus}} [same place]; ταῖς παρὰ τὴν ἀξίαν νῦν κακοπαθείαις your present unmerited **sufferings**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.77}}:—later, usually written **κᾰκοπαθ-παθία**, {{NT+3rd c.BC+|“IG” 22.900.16 (2nd c.BC), “SIG” 685.30 (Magnesia, 2nd c.BC), “BGU” 1209.7 (1st c.BC), NT.Jam.5.10: _plural_, “IG” 12(7).386.24 (Amorgos, 3rd c.BC), 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 86, etc.}}; **laborious toil, perseverance**, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|“BGU” [prev. cited] (1st c.BC).}}
2553:
** κᾰκοπαθ-έω**,
_future_ **-παθήσομαι**{{Refs 1st c.AD+|“PLond.” 1.98r73 (1st-2nd c.AD)}}: _perfect_ κεκακοπάθηκα {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 26.7}}:—**to be in ill plight, be in distress**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.78, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.1.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.26, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 6.28, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.146}}; πολλὰ κ. {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PCair.Zen.” 93.17 (3rd c.BC)}}; τινι **by** or **from** a thing, τοῦ Χωρίου τῇ ἀπορίᾳ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.29; ὑπό τινος [prev. author] 2.41; πρός τι 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ οἰκονομίας” p.53 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus}}; of sickness, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀρχαίης ἰητρικῇς” 19}}; κ. σώματι **suffer in** body, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.2, 18, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.46; τῇ ψυχῇ 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 191}}; of plants or trees, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 3.4.4, +others}}
2555:
** κᾰκοποι-ός**, όν,
**doing ill, mischievous**, ὄνειδος {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 8.33}}; σκεῦος, of a man, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 15.25.1}}; κακοποιοί **evil-doers**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1125a18}}; especially of poisoners and sorcerers, {{NT|NT.1Pet.4.15}}; of things, **noxious**, Χυλός {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 2.6.4, etc.; φάρμακα “PSI” 1.64.21 (1st c.BC)}}; τὸ κ. [τῆς ὕλης] {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 192a15}}: Astrology texts, **maleficent**, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 19, 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 4.59, etc.}}
2558:
** κᾰκουχ-έω**,
(ἔχω) **wrong, injure**, αὑτόν Telesp.34H.; **maltreat**, especially a wife, Mitteis{{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“Chr.” 284.6 (2nd c.BC), “POxy.” 281.17 (1st c.AD)}}, etc.:— _passive_, **to be afflicted** or **injured**, {{LXX+1st c.BC+|LXX.3Ki.2.26; ὑπὸ τοῦ δηγμοῦ 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.23; κακουχουμένους τελευτῆσαι τὸν βίον 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.114e.}}
2565:

2574:
** κάμηλος** [ᾰ], ὁ
and ἡ (as in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1563)}}, **camel, Camelus bactrianus** and **C. dromedarius** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|compare (4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 499a13), 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 285, etc.}}; τοὺς ἔρσενας τῶν κ. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.105}}; κ. ἀμνός **a camel**-lamb, i.e. young camel, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 1559 (Lyric poetry); κ. δρομάς 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 31: proverbial, κάμηλον καταπίνειν NT.Matt.23.24}}; compare κάμιλος.
**2** ἡ κ. **camelry**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.80}}. (Semitic word, cf. Hebrew **gāmāl.**)
2575:
** κάμῑν-ος** [ᾰ], ἡ,
**oven, furnace**, or **kiln**, for smelting, baking, burning earthenware and bricks, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus “Epigrammata” 14, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.179, 4.164, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 281, 5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus 2.13 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, “PPetr.” 3p.141 (3rd c.BC)}}, etc.: _plural_, of Hephaestus' forge, {{Refs|“Anacreontea” 27 A2}} **flue** for warming a room, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.332}}, compare 10.843; **alcove**, {{LXX|LXX.Num.25.8}}: proverbial of one who ate hot dishes, κάμινος οὐκ ἄνθρωπος {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Crobylus Comicus 8}}; κάμινον ἔχων ἐν τῷ πνεύμονι, of a drunkard, {{Refs|“Comica Adespota” 633. (Perh. _cognate_ with καμάρα, which see)}}
2576:
** καμμύω**,
_Epic dialect_ for καταμύω, variant in {{Refs|Batrachomyomachia 191}}: also in later Gr., τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐκάμμυσαν {{LXX+2nd c.BC+|LXX.Isa.6.10, +others, compare 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.645, 2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “Automatopoetica” 22.1, “PMag.Lond.” 121.855 (3rd c.AD), 7th c.AD: Paulus Aegineta Medicus 3.22.29}}: _perfect_ κεκάμμυκα {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 323.22: cited from 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 319 by 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista, but censured as un- 2nd c.AD: Atticus Philosophus}}

2592:
** καρποφορ-έω**,
**bear fruit**, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “de Vectigalibus” 1.3, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 755b10, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.602, +others, 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Fragmenta” 255: _metaphorically_, of virtue, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.154; τῷ θεῷ NT.Rom.7.4; also τῷ θανάτῳ [prev. work] 5}}:—_middle_, {{NT|NT.Col.1.6, “BMus.Inscription” 918 (Halic.)}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 80.}}
2593:
** καρποφόρ-ος**
(_paroxytone_), ον, **fruit-bearing, fruitful**, of trees, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.193, 2.156, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.22, etc.}}; of lands, Λιβύα, πεδία, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.6, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1485 (Lyric poetry); τῇ κ. γαίῃ “Sammelb.” 6598 (3rd c.AD), +others}}; of Demeter, τὴν κ. βασίλειαν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 384 (Lyric poetry), compare 2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 8.53.7, “CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 4082 (from Pessinus), “IG” 12(5).226 (from Paros), “SIG” 820.5 (Ephesus, 1st c.AD)}}: hence of Agrippina, {{NT|“IG” 12(2).212 (from Mytilene), “IGRom.” 4.1300 (Aeolis, in _feminine_ -φόρα); κ. καιροί NT.Act.14.17.}}
2599:
** καταβᾰρ-έω**,
**weigh down, overload**, variant for{καταπονέω} in {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DDeor.” 21.1}}: _metaphorically_, **impose a burden on**, τινας {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.2Cor.12.16; κ. τὴν Ἰταλίαν ἐσφοραῖς 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Bella Civilia” 5.67; ἀθληταὶ -βαροῦσι τοὺς τεχνίτας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Cleomenes” 27}}; τῶν -βαρούντων τὸ σῶμα καμάτων Ps.-{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Vitae Homeri” 207}}:—_passive_, **to be overborne, crushed**, καταβαρεῖσθαι τῇ μάχῃ {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 11.33.3; τοῖς ὅλοις [prev. author] 18.21.8; ὑπὸ τοῦ πάθους 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.24; ἐν ταῖς λειτουργίαις “POxy.” 487.10 (2nd c.AD)}}; also, **to be outweighed**, ὑπὸ τοῦ συμφέροντος {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.22.18.}}
